comparison: Both address post-entry restriction claims (C1, C2, C14). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising critical concerns that punctate SINV E1 staining indicates endosomal trapping rather than general post-entry restriction, suggesting authors missed an important mechanistic clue.

Both evaluate RNAi screen findings identifying restriction pathways (C3, C4, C5, C15). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on strong knockdown effects. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting these findings as 'novel insights' and 'important contribution' without challenge.

Both address A51R identification as rescue factor (C6, C16-C18, C77-C80). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with convergent evidence from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly acknowledging A51R identification as 'a surprising discovery' and key finding without challenging the experimental evidence.

Both evaluate microtubule stabilization claims (C9, C10, C24-C27, C89-C91). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on confocal microscopy and immunofluorescence data. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting findings without challenge and acknowledging A51R's association with microtubules.

Both address mass spectrometry interaction data (C11, C29, C94, C95). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while noting functional significance remains undetermined. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging A51R associates with microtubules and ubiquitin, noting these targets will be useful for future work.

Both evaluate protein stability claims (C12, C13, C30, C31, C96-C98). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on radiolabeling pulse-chase experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 explicitly challenging the evidence as 'not convincing,' noting lower protein levels could be due to decreased replication rather than stability, requesting proper pulse-chase experiments.

Both address separation-of-function mutant R321A (C28, C92, C93). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, calling this critical for demonstrating MT stabilization doesn't explain rescue. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this as valid clue to mechanism without challenge.

Both evaluate vertebrate cell replication defects (C7, C32, C99, C100). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on growth curve analyses. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging VACV lacking functional A51R is attenuated without raising concerns about the data.

Both address mouse pathogenesis and virulence (C8, C33, C34, C101-C105). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on survival differences and tissue-specific titers. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting attenuation and potential importance for vaccine strains without challenging the data.

Both evaluate A51R homolog conservation across poxviruses (C21, C84, C85). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on LUC assays showing broad functional conservation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting conservation findings as part of A51R characterization.

Both address specificity to Lepidopteran cells (C22, C86-C88). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on cell line comparisons. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting LD652 will likely become system of choice for investigating antiviral immunity in Lepidoptera.

Both address Lepidoptera vs Drosophila specificity (C23). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on lack of effect in DL1 cells. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this specificity as consistent with overall experimental findings.

Both evaluate EEV release findings (C35, C106). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting paradoxically increased EEV despite lower titers rules out EEV deficiency. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this as part of ΔA51R phenotype characterization without comment.

Both address IFN sensitivity (C36, C107, C108). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on equivalent reduction in titers for both strains. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this rules out increased IFN sensitivity as mechanism of attenuation.

Both address cell viability/productive replication (C20). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on transfection experiments showing productive viral replication. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this without comment as consistent with restored replication.

Both address VACV overcoming established restriction (C68). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as part of post-entry restriction evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this finding supports overall conclusion about VACV rescue capability.

Both evaluate speculative mechanistic hypotheses (C62-C67). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but untested hypotheses appropriately presented as possibilities. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging mechanism is 'still vague' with Reviewer 1's endosomal trapping concern suggesting need to re-examine mechanistic proposals.

OpenEval R16 addresses differential VSV vs SINV rescue (C81), rating SUPPORTED while noting additional factors contribute to SINV rescue. Peer R3 addresses broader A51R identification (C6, C16-C19, C77-C81 including C81), rating SUPPORTED and acknowledging A51R as key discovery.

OpenEval R5 addresses A51R transfection rescue experiments (C19, C82, C83, C20), rating SUPPORTED. Peer R3 addresses broader A51R identification including C19, rating SUPPORTED and acknowledging A51R's rescue capability as surprising discovery.

OpenEval R3 addresses specificity of restriction to cytoplasmically-replicating viruses vs plasmid-driven expression (C71-C73), rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about mechanism specificity.

OpenEval R17 addresses contextual/background claims from prior work (C37-C59, C61), rating SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these are background claims rather than novel findings being evaluated.
